IS : 11566 - 1986 




Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
VALVE RETRACTORS 



( Reaffirmed 2002 ) 



1. Scope — This standard specifies material, dimensions and other requirements for valve retractors 
used in cardiovascular surgery. 

2. Material — Stainless steel conforming to Designation 20Cr13 or 30Cr13 of 13:6603-1972 
'Specification for stainless steel bars and flats'.

3.1 Tolerances on various dimensions shall be as follows: 

a) =b 0*05 mm on dimensions up to 20 mm, 

b) ± 0*1 mm on dimensions above 20 mm and up to 5 mm, 

c) ± 0'2 mm on dimensions above 5"0 mm and up to 200 mm, 

d) ± 0*5 mm on dimensions above 200 mm and up to 500 mm, 

e) VO mm on dimensions above 500 mm and up to 1000 mm, and 

f) ±, 20 mm on dimensions above 100*0 mm. 

4. Heat Treatment — The retractors shall be evenly hardened and tempered to give a hardness 
of 400 to 460 HV, when tested in accordance with IS : 1501 ( Part 1 )-1984 'Method for Vickers hardness 
test for metallic materials; Part 1 HV 5 to HV 100 ( second revision )'. 

5. Workmanship 

5.1 The handle shall be knurled, if required by the purchaser. 

5.2 All the edges and corners, except knurled handle, shall be properly rounded. 

6. Surface Condition 

6.1 General— AU surfaces shall be free from pores, crevices and grinding marks. The Instrument shall 
be supplied free from residual scale, acid, grease and grinding and polishing materials. Compliance 
with these requirements shall be checked by inspection using normal vision ( corrected, if necessary). 

6.2 Surface Finish — The surface finish shall be one of, or a combination of, the following: 

a) Reflection-reducing, for example, satin finish, matt black finish; and 

b) An applied surface coating, for example, for insulation purposes. 

Note — The satin finish should be effected by an appropriate procedure, such as grinding, brushing, 
electropollshing and, in addition, satin finishing (glass beading or satin brushing). The finish should be 
uniform and smooth and It should reduce glare- 



IS - 11566-1986 

6,3 Passivation and Final Treatment —The instrument shall be treated by a suitable passivation 
process. 

Note 1 — Examples of methods of passivation are by electropoiishing or by treating wltii 10 percent {vj*/) 
nitric acid solution for not less than 30 minutes at a temperature not less than 10°C and not exceeding 60°C. 
The retractor should then be rinsed in water and dried in hot air. 

Note 2 — If the joint is lubricated, the lubricant should be non-corrosive and suitable for medical application 
according to the Indian Pharmacopoeia. 

7. Tests 

7.1 Rigidity Test 

7.1.1 The retracting part of the blade shall be applied to the edge of a chair or table. It shall be 
pulled manually by applying a maximum force along the axis of the handle. The retractor shall show 
no sign of damage or permanent set. 

7.1.2 A load of 25 kg shall be suspended from the top of the turned end of the retracting blade. 
The maximum load shall be gradually attained and maintained for 2 minutes. On completion of the 
test, the retractor snail show no sign of damage. 

7.2 Corrosion Resistance Test — The instrument shall be tested in accordance with IS: 7531-1975 
'Method for boiling and autoclaving test for corrosion resistance of stainless steel surgical 
instruments'. It shall show no sign of corrosion after the test. 

8. Marking — The retractors shall be clearly and indelibly marked, preferably by etching, with the 
following: 

a) Manufacturer's name, initials or recognized trade-mark; 

b) Pattern and, where applicable, size of the retractor; and 

c) The words 'stainless steel' or letters 'SS'. 

8.1 ISI Certification l\/larking — Details available with the Indian Standards Institution. 

9. Packing —The retractors may be packed as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. 

10. Sampling — Sampling procedure and acceptance criteria for the retractors shall be as agreed to 
between the purchaser and the supplier. A recommended scheme for the same is given in 
Appendix A. 



APPENDIX A 

{Clause 10) 

SAMPLING SCHEME AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY 
FOR VALVE RETRACTORS 

A-1- Lot— In any consignment, ail the retractors of the same pattern and size, produced from the 
same material under similar conditions shall constitute a lot. 

A-2. The number of retractors to be selected from each lot shall depend upon the size of the lot and 
shall be in accordance with col 1 and 2 of Table 1.

A-2.1 These retractors shall be selected from the lot at random and in order to ensure randomness of

A-3. Numb«r of Tetts and Criteria for Conformity 

A-3.1 All the retractors selected at random in accordance with col 1 and 2 of Table 1 shall be 
examined for shape and dimensions^ workmanship and surface condition ( visual ). None of the 
retractors in the sample shall fail to meet any of these requirements if the lot is to be accepted under 
this clause. 

A-3.2 A sub-sample of size given in col 3 of Table 1 shall be selected at random from the retractors 
drawn as in A-2. The instruments in the sub-sampie shall be subjected to hardness, rigidity and 
corrosion resistance tests. No failure shall occur in any of these tests if the lot is to be accepted under 
this clause.
